text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is causing your discomfort, can you tell me if you have been vomiting, and if so, is the vomit ever green or yellow?

text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor

The crying when your belly is touched suggests significant pain; is there any history of constipation, or have you noticed ribbon-like stools? Also, have you had any episodes of intense, colicky crying followed by periods of calm?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The clinical presentation of intermittent severe pain, drawing up of legs, and abdominal distension, combined with the X-ray findings of a distal obstruction, is highly suggestive of this condition in an 8-month-old.
